To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Co-production of assisted living technologies and services requires the active involvement of users and carers in the development process.
the low uptake of telehealth and assisted living services by older people can be explained by their limited involvement in the design of these technologies and services.

1) co-production workshops are a powerful means to engage people with assisted living (ALT) needs and their carers with technology and service designers, 2) ALT users need to be supported in the use of the technology, 3) the technology needs to be customisable to accommodate the multiple needs of users and 4) the technology needs support from the wider social support network of the user.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to co-produce new technologies and services that can support the evolving needs of older people and their carers in the home environment.
the social, rather than the technical, design of ALTs.
how to co-produce new technologies and services that are more likely to be used by older people.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the co-design process is not only an important tool for the design of technology, but also an opportunity to explore the social processes that underpin the delivery of care and the use of technology in the home.
the co-design workshops identified a need for a greater focus on the social aspects of technology design and service delivery.
co-design workshops can be used to explore the design of telecare and assistive technologies, but they need to be carefully planned and managed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the co-design process can help to identify the social processes that need to be in place to support the use of technology and the service delivery.
co-design is a useful approach for involving users of assisted living technology and services in the design and evaluation of these technologies and services.
we have developed a new model for the co-production of technology and services for people with assisted living (AL) needs, and that this model can be applied across the AL sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the social processes and relationships that underpin care are at least as important as the technology itself in enabling the successful co-design and delivery of ALTs.
ALTs should be co-designed by all the key actors involved in their use, and that co-design workshops are one means to achieve this.
co-design workshops can provide an opportunity to develop new ways of thinking about the design of ALTs and services that are more inclusive of users.
